tldr: Headlines across all 29 national buckets lock onto a single emergency register — death tolls (500–600 dead), missing-person counts (1,500–2,500), and the ongoing secondary flood threat from barrier lakes — making this one of the most convergent headline corpora in the dataset. A secondary layer of UK tabloids, Qatar, Philippines, and Canada foregrounds family grief and survivor testimony rather than statistics. Chinese state headlines uniquely pivot to Xi Jinping's party leadership directives, while a small climate cluster in Asia-Pacific and opinion outlets reframes the disaster as a Himalayan climate security warning. Nepal's sovereignty decision to decline foreign rescue teams surfaces as a discrete policy sub-story across wire, South Asian, and Pakistani buckets.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Most sensational framing in the corpus: leads headline with 'LIVE', death count, and a vivid footage description ('people fleeing before floodwaters hit settlement and destroy it in minutes') — an eyewitness-action frame absent from all other outlets.
Only outlet to label this disaster a 'Climate Security Warning' in the headline itself, foregrounding geopolitical-climate risk rather than rescue or death-toll metrics.
Only outlet to pivot the headline from disaster response to a bilateral transparency question: 'Will China Consider Sharing Risk Info With Neighbours' — a unique geopolitical data-sovereignty angle.

bottom_line: The headline layer presents a nearly uniform emergency frame — dead, missing, second flood looming — with Chinese state outlets and a small climate cluster as the only significant departures from the global consensus register.
